The male bird-of-paradise puts on a strange dance and shows off fancy feathers just to impress the female.
copy.tl:
Bakit sumasayaw ang bird-of-paradise?

Nagsasayaw ng kakaiba ang lalaking bird-of-paradise at ipinapakita ang magandang balahibo niya para humanga ang babae.
copy.bis:
Nganong mosayaw ang bird-of-paradise?

Mosayaw og talagsaon ang lalaki nga bird-of-paradise ug ipakita ang iyang matahom nga balhibo aron madani ang baye.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Birds have a large breastbone called a keel, where their strong flight muscles attach so they can fly.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The competency focuses on outer body parts (head, legs, wings) and their role in movement and food gathering. The keel is an internal breastbone, not an outer body part, and the card does not describe any outer part or its role in gathering food. It only relates to flight movement via an internal structure.

copy.en: Birds have a large breastbone called a keel, where their strong flight muscles attach so they can fly.
copy.tl: May malaking butong-dibdib ang ibon na tinatawag na keel, kung saan nakakabit ang malalakas na kalamnan para makalipad.
copy.bis: Ang langgam adunay dako nga bukog sa dughan nga gitawag og keel, diin nasangit ang kusgan nga kaunoran aron makalupad.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: feathers also keep a bird's body warm
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes feathers, an outer body part, but focuses on their role in keeping the bird warm, not on movement or gathering food as required by the competency. The competency specifically asks for roles related to moving and gathering food, which this card does not address.

copy.en: Besides helping birds fly, feathers also keep a bird's body warm even in cold weather.
copy.tl: Bukod sa paglipad, ang balahibo rin ang nagpapanatiling mainit sa katawan ng ibon kahit malamig.
copy.bis: Gawas sa pagtabang sa paglupad, ang balhibo usab maoy nagpabilin nga init sa lawas sa langgam bisan bugnaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When a bird pushes its wings downward, that's where the strongest force comes from to lift up and move forward
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to demonstrate that pushes and pulls can be used to change the speed and direction of an object including making it go faster, turn it to a different direction, slow it down, and stop it
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a bird's downstroke as a push that produces lift and forward motion, but it does not demonstrate how pushes/pulls change speed or direction (faster, slower, turn, stop). It is a single example of force causing motion, not an activity or demonstration of changing speed/direction.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When a bird pushes its wings downward, that's where the strongest force comes from to lift up and move forward
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out simple investigations to demonstrate that contact forces cause objects to move in the same direction as the direction that the force is applied
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a push (downstroke) causing motion, but it does not address contact forces causing objects to move in the same direction as the applied force, nor does it involve a simple investigation. The bird's wing push is a contact force example, but the card does not explicitly connect the direction of force to the direction of motion or support the investigative skill.

copy.en:
Where does a bird get its strongest flying power?

From the downstroke! When a bird pushes its wings downward, that's where the strongest force comes from to lift up and move forward—like a powerful paddle stroke!
copy.tl:
Saan nagmumula ang pinakamalakas na puwersa ng ibon sa paglipad?

Sa downstroke! Kapag ibinababa ng ibon ang pakpak nito, doon nagmumula ang pinakamalakas na puwersa para mag-angat at sumulong—parang malakas na pagsagwan!
copy.bis:
Asal gikan ang labing kusog nga puwersa sa langgam sa paglupad?

Sa downstroke! Kon ibutang sa langgam ang iyang pako paubos, didto magagikan ang labing kusog nga puwersa aron mosaka ug mopadayon—sama sa kusog nga pagbugsay!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Not all birds can fly! Some, like the ostrich, run on the ground instead of flying.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions birds and the ostrich but does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups. It only gives a single fact about flightless birds, so it does not directly support the classification competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Not all birds can fly! Some, like the ostrich, run on the ground instead of flying.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to an animal's movement (running instead of flying) but does not observe or describe outer body parts such as head, legs, or wings, nor identify their role in moving and gathering food. It is only tangentially related to animal body parts and movement.

copy.en:
Can all birds fly?

Not all birds can fly! Some, like the ostrich, run on the ground instead of flying.
copy.tl:
Lahat ba ng ibon ay nakakalipad?

Hindi lahat ng ibon ay nakakalipad! Ang ilan tulad ng ostrich ay tumatakbo sa lupa sa halip na lumipad.
copy.bis:
Makalupad ba ang tanang langgam?

Dili tanang langgam makalupad! Ang uban sama sa ostrich modagan sa yuta imbes molupad.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Even though a bird's bones are hollow, tiny crisscross struts inside keep them strong without adding extra weight.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the structural mechanism of hollow bird bones (struts) but does not frame it as an example of animals changing to better suit their environment, nor does it mention adaptation, flight, or environmental pressures. It is a fact about bird anatomy, not a description of an adaptive change.

copy.en:
How are hollow bird bones so strong?

Even though a bird's bones are hollow, tiny crisscross struts inside keep them strong without adding extra weight.
copy.tl:
Paano lumalakas ang guwang na buto ng ibon?

Kahit guwang ang buto ng ibon, may maliliit na suhay sa loob nito na nagpapatibay dito nang hindi nadaragdagan ang bigat.
copy.bis:
Giunsa paglig-on ang guwang nga bukog sa langgam?

Bisan guwang ang bukog sa langgam, adunay gagmay nga suhay sa sulod niini nga naglig-on niini nga walay dugang gibug-aton.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it can still break under too much force
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: determine how forces can change the shape of objects such as when they are pushed, pulled, stretched, bent, twisted, or squeezed
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that a bone can break under too much force, which touches on forces changing objects, but it does not describe how forces change the shape of objects (pushed, pulled, stretched, bent, twisted, squeezed). The focus is on bird bone strength and gentle handling, not on force effects on shape.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A bird's hollow bone has inner struts
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: G4-L-1 requires describing human body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory). The card discusses bird bones, not the human skeletal system, and provides no information about how any human body system works.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A bird's hollow bone has inner struts that make it strong
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a physical property (strength) of a solid material (bone), but it does not describe physical properties like hard, shiny, or stretchable in a general material sense. It is about a specific biological structure, not a general lesson on solid material properties.

copy.en:
Can a hollow bird bone still break?

A bird's hollow bone has inner struts that make it strong, but it can still break under too much force — so always handle birds gently.
copy.tl:
Madali bang mabali ang buto ng ibon?

May mga panloob na suporta ang guwang na buto ng ibon na nagpapatibay dito, pero kaya pa rin itong mabali kung sobra ang puwersa — kaya maging maingat sa paghawak ng ibon.
copy.bis:
Dali ba mabuak ang buto sa langgam?

Ang hawan nga buto sa langgam adunay suporta sa sulod nga naghimo niini nga lig-on, apan mahimo gihapon kining mabuak kung sobra ang kusog — busa pag-amping sa paghawid og langgam.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Birds have large, strong chest muscles that power the flapping of their wings.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The competency focuses on observing and describing outer body parts (head, legs, wings) and their role in movement and food gathering. The card describes internal chest muscles that power wing flapping, not an outer body part itself. It shares the topic of wings and movement but does not directly support describing outer body parts.

copy.en: Birds have large, strong chest muscles that power the flapping of their wings.
copy.tl: May malalaki at malalakas na kalamnan sa dibdib ang ibon na nagpapakilos sa mga pakpak nito.
copy.bis: Ang langgam adunay dagko ug kusgan nga kaunoran sa dughan nga nagpalihok sa iyang mga pako.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a bitter taste can actually warn your body that something might not be safe to eat
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not grow, respond, and reproduce as characteristics of living things.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many poisonous plants taste bitter
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe that living things interact with each other in the natural environment, such as through competition, or predation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not living things interacting through competition or predation.

copy.en:
Why might a bitter taste be a warning?

Many poisonous plants taste bitter, so a bitter taste can actually warn your body that something might not be safe to eat!
copy.tl:
Bakit maaaring babala ang mapait na lasa?

Karamihan sa mga nakakalasong halaman ay mapait, kaya nagsisilbing babala ang mapait na lasa sa katawan mo na baka hindi ligtas kainin!
copy.bis:
Nganong mahimong pasidaan ang pait nga lami?

Daghang makahilo nga tanom ang pait, mao nga ang pait nga lami mahimong pasidaan sa imong lawas nga tingali dili luwas kaonon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Black pepper comes from the small round berries of a climbing vine
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes black pepper as berries from a vine used as spice. It does not address the outer parts of plants (leaves, roots, stems) or their roles in obtaining water and nutrients, which is the focus of G3-L-5.

copy.en: Black pepper comes from the small round berries of a climbing vine, dried and used to spice up food.
copy.tl: Ang paminta ay galing sa maliliit at bilog na bunga ng isang gumagapang na baging na pinatutuyo at ginagawang pampalasa.
copy.bis: Ang paminta gikan sa gagmay ug lingin nga bunga sa nagakatay nga baging nga gipauga ug gigamit pampalami sa pagkaon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Urine made by the kidneys is stored in the bladder until it fills up and we need to pass it out.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a single fact about the bladder's storage function. It does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations, nor does it explain how body systems work together (e.g., digestion and excretion). It is only tangentially related to excretion.

copy.en: Urine made by the kidneys is stored in the bladder until it fills up and we need to pass it out.
copy.tl: Ang ihing ginawa ng mga bato ay iniimbak muna sa pantog hanggang mapuno ito at kailangan na nating umihi.
copy.bis: Ang ihi nga gihimo sa mga kidni gitipigan una sa tunggo hangtod mapuno kini ug kinahanglan na kitang moihi.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Columbidae — the same family as all pigeons and doves worldwide! Its genus is Gallicolumba.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states the family and genus of bleeding-heart doves but does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups (mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians, etc.). It only mentions a single bird's taxonomic placement, which is related to classification but does not directly support the competency's required table-based grouping.

copy.en:
What bird family do bleeding-heart doves belong to?

Columbidae — the same family as all pigeons and doves worldwide! Its genus is Gallicolumba.
copy.tl:
Anong pamilya ng ibon ang bleeding-heart dove?

Columbidae — ang pamilya ng lahat ng kalapati at kalyos sa buong mundo! Ang genus nito ay Gallicolumba.
copy.bis:
Unsang pamilya sa langgam sakop ang bleeding-heart dove?

Columbidae — ang pamilya sa tanang salampati sa kalibutan! Ang genus niini mao ang Gallicolumba.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: press a clean cloth firmly on it and hold steady pressure for several minutes so the blood can start to clot
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: First-aid clotting is adjacent to blood; the card does not identify heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: so the blood can start to clot
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: Wound pressure is first aid, not the five body systems as a set.

copy.en: To stop a wound from bleeding, press a clean cloth firmly on it and hold steady pressure for several minutes so the blood can start to clot.
copy.tl: Para mapatigil ang pagdurugo ng sugat, ipatong ang malinis na tela at pindutin nang mahigpit sa loob ng ilang minuto hanggang magsimulang mamuo ang dugo.
copy.bis: Aron mapahunong ang pagdugo sa sugat, ibutang ang limpyo nga tela ug pinduton ug maayo sulod sa pipila ka minuto aron magsugod ang pagmuo sa dugo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A blizzard is a strong snowstorm with very strong winds and lots of falling snow
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and record changes in the weather during a day or over some days and describe the different types and patterns of weather in the local area
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines a blizzard as a type of weather, but the competency requires observing and recording weather changes over time and describing types/patterns in the local area. The card provides no instruction on observation, recording, or local weather patterns; it only names a weather phenomenon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A blizzard is a strong snowstorm with very strong winds and lots of falling snow
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions strong winds and falling snow, which are weather characteristics, but it does not identify or explain the basic characteristics used to describe weather (air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, cloud cover). It merely describes a blizzard without linking to the listed characteristics or their measurement.

copy.en: A blizzard is a strong snowstorm with very strong winds and lots of falling snow, making it hard to see anything around you!
copy.tl: Ang blizzard ay malakas na bagyong niyebe na may napakalakas na hangin at maraming bumabagsak na niyebe, kaya halos hindi na makita ang paligid!
copy.bis: Ang blizzard usa ka kusog nga bagyo sa niyebe nga adunay kusog kaayo nga hangin ug daghang nahulog nga niyebe, mao nga halos dili na makita ang palibot!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because you remove the protection before the skin underneath finishes healing!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that cells reproduce through two types of cell division, mitosis and meiosis, and describe mitosis as cell division for growth and repair
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses why picking a scab is harmful, mentioning skin healing, bleeding, infection, and scarring. It does not mention cell division, mitosis, meiosis, or the role of mitosis in growth and repair. The healing concept is only tangentially related to cellular reproduction, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Why shouldn't you pick at a scab?

Because you remove the protection before the skin underneath finishes healing! This can make it bleed again, get infected, or leave a scar.
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi dapat kinakalkal ang langib?

Dahil tinatanggal mo ang proteksyon bago pa man matapos gumaling ang balat! Pwede itong magdugo ulit, magkaroon ng impeksyon, o mag-iwan ng peklat.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga dili angay kalkalon ang langib?

Kay imong gikuha ang panalipod sa wala pa mahuman pag-ayo ang panit sa ilalom! Mahimo kining modugo pag-usab, matakdan og impeksyon, o mobilin og peklat.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Healthy people can donate blood to help sick or injured patients who need it
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Donating blood is a social practice, not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

copy.en: Healthy people can donate blood to help sick or injured patients who need it.
copy.tl: Ang malulusog na tao ay maaaring magbigay ng dugo para tumulong sa mga maysakit o nasugatang nangangailangan nito.
copy.bis: Ang himsog nga mga tawo makahatag og dugo aron motabang sa masakiton o nasamdan nga nanginahanglan niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: problems can arise when the mother is Rh-negative but her baby is Rh-positive
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: represent patterns of inheritance of a simple dominant/ recessive characteristic through generations of a family
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions Rh factor, which is inherited as a dominant/recessive trait, but it does not teach how to represent inheritance patterns through generations. It only describes a pregnancy complication, providing no pedigree, family generations, or dominant/recessive representation.

copy.en: During pregnancy, Rh factor matters too — problems can arise when the mother is Rh-negative but her baby is Rh-positive.
copy.tl: Mahalaga rin ang Rh factor sa pagbubuntis — maaaring magkaproblema kapag Rh-negative ang ina pero Rh-positive ang sanggol.
copy.bis: Importante usab ang Rh factor sa pagmabdos — mahimong magkaproblema kon Rh-negative ang inahan apan Rh-positive ang bata.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the donor's and patient's blood types must match, or the blood could cause harm
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Matching types for transfusion is clinical practice, not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the donor's and patient's blood types must match
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: Transfusion matching is not the five body systems as a set.

copy.en: In a blood transfusion, the donor's and patient's blood types must match, or the blood could cause harm.
copy.tl: Sa pagsasalin ng dugo, dapat magtugma ang uri ng dugo ng nagbigay at tumanggap para hindi ito makasama.
copy.bis: Sa pag-salin og dugo, kinahanglang mohaom ang klase sa dugo sa naghatag ug sa nagdawat aron dili kini makadaot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a person's blood type never changes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of DNA, genes, and chromosomes in the transmission of traits
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that blood type is fixed for life but does not mention DNA, genes, chromosomes, or how traits are transmitted. It shares the genetics topic but provides no instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a person's blood type never changes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: represent patterns of inheritance of a simple dominant/ recessive characteristic through generations of a family
assignedReviews.reason: Blood type is an inherited characteristic, but the card only asserts that it does not change over a lifetime. It does not represent inheritance patterns, dominant/recessive relationships, or family generations, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Does your blood type ever change?

Nope — a person's blood type never changes. Whatever type you were born with stays the same your whole life.
copy.tl:
Nagbabago ba ang uri ng dugo mo?

Hindi pala! Ang uri ng dugo ng tao ay hindi nagbabago at nananatiling pareho habambuhay.
copy.bis:
Nausab ba ang imong klase sa dugo?

Dili diay! Ang klase sa dugo sa tawo dili mausab ug magpabilin nga pareho sa tibuok kinabuhi.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: AB positive (AB+) — a person with this blood type can receive blood from anyone
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Universal-recipient typing is transfusion practice, not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: can receive blood from anyone
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: Transfusion typing is not the five body systems as a set.

copy.en:
Which blood type is the universal recipient?

AB positive (AB+) — a person with this blood type can receive blood from anyone.
copy.tl:
Anong uri ng dugo ang tinatawag na universal recipient?

Ang AB positive (AB+) — kaya nitong tumanggap ng dugo mula sa kahit sinong donor.
copy.bis:
Unsa nga klase sa dugo ang gitawag og universal recipient?

Ang AB positive (AB+) — makadawat kini og dugo gikan sa bisan kinsa nga donor.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: there are eight blood types in total: A+, A−, B+, B−, AB+, AB−, O+, and O−
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Counting Rh blood types is typing trivia, not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

copy.en: Count in the Rh factor and there are eight blood types in total: A+, A−, B+, B−, AB+, AB−, O+, and O−.
copy.tl: Kapag isinama ang Rh positive at negative, may walong uri ng dugo lahat-lahat: A+, A−, B+, B−, AB+, AB−, O+, at O−.
copy.bis: Kung iapil ang Rh positive ug negative, adunay walo ka klase sa dugo tanan: A+, A−, B+, B−, AB+, AB−, O+, ug O−.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Blue light is scattered most easily by tiny bits of air
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a specific behavior of light (scattering) but does not address sources of light, how light can be changed, or its uses in everyday situations, nor does it involve guided science activities. It shares vocabulary about light but does not directly support the competency's instructional goals.

copy.en: The sky is blue because sunlight has many colors! Blue light is scattered most easily by tiny bits of air, and that scattered blue is what we see everywhere.
copy.tl: Asul ang langit dahil maraming kulay ang sikat ng araw! Ang asul na liwanag ay mas madaling makalat ng mga butil ng hangin, kaya iyon ang nakikita natin sa buong langit.
copy.bis: Asul ang langit kay daghang kulay ang silaw sa adlaw! Ang asul nga kahayag mas sayon makatag sa gagmay nga tipik sa hangin, mao nga kana ang atong makita sa tibuok langit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It can weigh up to about 150 tons
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and appropriately use units in simple science activities, such as milligrams (mg), grams (g), kilograms (kg), and degrees centigrade (C)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a unit of mass (tons) but does not teach identifying or appropriately using units in simple science activities, nor does it involve the listed units (mg, g, kg, °C) or any measurement activity.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The blue whale! It can weigh up to about 150 tons
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the blue whale's weight, not about classifying Philippine animals/plants by habitat using a drawing or diagram. The blue whale is not a Philippine animal in the context of this competency, and no habitat classification or drawing/diagram is present.

copy.en:
What's the heaviest animal ever?

The blue whale! It can weigh up to about 150 tons — heavier than any other animal on Earth.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamabigat na hayop?

Ang blue whale! Umaabot ito sa halos 150 tonelada ang bigat — mas mabigat pa sa kahit anong hayop sa Earth.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakabug-at nga mananap?

Ang blue whale! Makaabot kini ug halos 150 ka tonelada ang gibug-aton — mas bug-at pa sa bisan unsang mananap sa Yuta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It can weigh up to about 150 tonnes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and appropriately use units in simple science activities, such as milligrams (mg), grams (g), kilograms (kg), and degrees centigrade (C)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions weight in tonnes, but the competency requires identifying and appropriately using units like mg, g, kg, and °C in simple science activities. The card does not teach unit identification, conversion, or appropriate use; it only states a factual weight.

copy.en:
What's the heaviest animal on Earth?

It's the blue whale! It can weigh up to about 150 tonnes — the heaviest animal there is.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamabigat na hayop sa mundo?

Ang blue whale! Kaya nitong tumimbang ng hanggang 150 tonelada — ang pinakamabigat na hayop.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakabug-at nga mananap sa kalibotan?

Ang blue whale! Mahimo kining motimbang ug hangtod 150 ka tonelada — ang pinakabug-at nga mananap.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the paddle is your way back to shore
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe examples and uses of simple machines found at home, at school, and in the community
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a paddle, which is a simple machine, but it does not describe its use as a simple machine, its mechanical advantage, or any example of simple machines in the community. It only frames the paddle as a safety backup, so it does not directly support the competency of observing and describing examples and uses of simple machines.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why do motorized boats still carry a paddle as a backup even when they have an engine?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life

Nganong nagdala gihapon ug bugsay isip reserba ang mga makinahon nga bangka bisan adunay makina na?

Reserba kini para sa kaluwasan! Kon mahurot ang gasolina o madaot ang makina sa dagat, ang bugsay ang pabalik sa baybayon. Busa importante gihapon ang kahibalo sa pagbugsay.

Can boiling hard water make it softer?

Yes! Boiling some kinds of hard water helps soften it because the minerals settle out as a deposit.

Pwede bang palambutin ang matigas na tubig sa pamamagitan ng pagpapakulo?

Oo! Nakakatulong ang pagpapakulo sa ilang uri ng matigas na tubig na lumambot dahil bumababa ang mineral bilang latak.

Mahimo bang pahumokon ang gahi nga tubig pinaagi sa pagpabukal?

Oo! Makatabang ang pagpabukal sa pipila ka klase sa gahi nga tubig nga mohumok kay mahulog ang mineral isip latak.

The white blood cells that defend your body are made inside your bones, in a part called the bone marrow.

Ang mga puting selula ng dugo na tagapagtanggol ay ginagawa sa loob ng buto, sa bahaging tinatawag na bone marrow.

Asa gihimo ang puti nga selula sa dugo?

Ang puti nga selula sa dugo nga tigpanalipod gihimo sulod sa bukog, sa bahin nga gitawag og bone marrow.

How many bones are in one foot?

One human foot has 26 bones — that's a lot packed into one small part of your body!

Ilang buto meron ang isang paa?

Ang isang paa ng tao ay may 26 na buto — dami nito para sa isang maliit na bahagi ng katawan!

Ang usa ka tiil sa tawo adunay 26 ka bukog — daghan gyud para sa gamay ra nga bahin sa lawas!

What does bougainvillea's real flower look like?

It's tiny, white, and trumpet-shaped — usually three grow together, hidden inside the colorful bracts we mistake for the flower!

Ano ang hitsura ng totoong bulaklak ng bougainvillea?

Maliit, puti, at hugis-trumpeta ito — karaniwang tatlo ang magkasamang tumutubo, nakatago sa loob ng makukulay na bracts na akala natin ay bulaklak!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang hitsura sa tinuod nga bulak sa bougainvillea?

Gamay, puti, ug porma'g trumpeta kini — kasagaran tulo ang magkuyog og tubo, natago sa sulod sa kolorado nga bracts nga atong gituohang bulak!

Which sea animal has 24 real eyes?

Aling hayop-dagat ang may 24 na tunay na mata?

Ang box jellyfish ay isa sa pinaka-delikadong hayop sa dagat — mayroon itong tunay na mga mata (24 sa apat na cluster!) at ang lason nito ay kayang pumatay sa tao sa loob lang ng ilang minuto.

Unsang hayop sa dagat ang adunay 24 ka tinuod nga mata?

Ang box jellyfish usa sa pinaka-delikadong mga hayop sa dagat — adunay tinuod nga mga mata (24 sa upat ka cluster!) ug ang hilo niini makapatay sa tawo sulod lang og pipila ka minuto.

Where a river flows into the sea, the water becomes brackish — a little salty — because fresh water and salt water mix together.

Bakit medyo-alat ang tubig doon?

Kung saan nagtatagpo ang ilog at dagat, nagiging medyo-alat o brackish ang tubig dahil naghahalo ang tabang at alat na tubig.
copy.bis:
Nganong tunga-tunga og asin ang tubig didto?

Sa dapit nga magtagbo ang suba ug dagat, mahimong tunga-tunga og asin ang tubig kay nagsagol ang tab-ang ug parat nga tubig.

Can your brain do many things at once?

Almost! Breathing, walking, listening, and thinking happen together because different brain parts work at once — but two attention-heavy tasks together slow you down.

Halos oo! Sabay na nangyayari ang paghinga, paglakad, pakikinig, at pag-iisip dahil iba't ibang bahagi ng utak ang sabay-sabay na gumagana — pero kapag dalawang bagay na kailangan ng atensyon ang sabay mong ginagawa, bumabagal ka pareho.
copy.bis:
Makahimo ba ang utok og daghang butang nga dungan?

Halos oo! Dungan nga mahitabo ang pagginhawa, paglakaw, pagpaminaw, ug paghunahuna tungod kay lain-laing bahin sa utok ang dungan nga nagtrabaho — apan kon duha ka buluhaton nga nanginahanglan og atensyon ang dungan nimong buhaton, mohinay ka sa duha.

What does the brain control?

The brain is the control center of the nervous system — it's where you think, remember, and feel, and where commands to move your body come from.

Ang utak ang sentro ng nervous system — dito nangyayari ang pag-iisip, pag-alaala, at pakiramdam, at dito rin nagmumula ang utos na gumagalaw sa katawan.
copy.bis:
Unsay buhaton sa utok?

Ang utok mao ang sentro sa nervous system — dinhi mahitabo ang panghunahuna, paghinumdom, ug pagbati, ug dinhi usab gikan ang mando nga naglihok sa lawas.

copy.tl:
Bakit may iba't ibang kulay ng balahibo ang ilang tuta mula sa parehong magulang?

Ang pagkakaiba sa kulay ng balahibo, kulay ng mata, at taas ay maaaring resulta ng iba't ibang pagpaparami!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga ang uban nga mga itoy nga pareho og ginikanan adunay lain-laing kolor sa balahibo?

Ang kalainan sa kolor sa balahibo, kolor sa mata, ug gitas-on mahimong resulta sa lain-laing pagpasanay!

copy.tl:
Paano hinahawakan ng suspension bridge ang kalsada nito?

Inibibitay nito ang kalsada gamit ang mga cable sa mataas na towers! Nasa tension ang mga cable para pasanin ang bigat ng tulay.
copy.bis:
Giunsa paghupot sa suspension bridge ang dalan niini?

Gibitay niini ang dalan gamit ang mga cable sa taas nga mga tore! Naa sa tension ang mga cable aron pasanin ang gibug-aton sa tulay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A broken bone usually hurts a lot, swells up, and becomes hard to move
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes symptoms of a broken bone, which is a skeletal system injury, but it does not describe how the skeletal system (or any other body system) works. It provides no information about the function, structure, or operation of the skeletal system, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: A broken bone usually hurts a lot, swells up, and becomes hard to move — those are the telltale signs.
copy.tl: Kapag may baling buto, kadalasan ay masakit, namamaga, at mahirap nang igalaw ang bahaging iyon.
copy.bis: Kung adunay bali nga bukog, kasagaran sakit kaayo, mohubag, ug lisod na ilihok ang maong bahin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bronze is a classic alloy made by mixing copper and tin (lata) together to make it strong!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that bronze is an alloy made from copper and tin. It does not describe uniform versus non-uniform mixtures, nor does it give examples such as solutions and suspensions. The alloy fact is topically related to mixtures but does not directly support the competency's required skill.

copy.en:
What two metals combine to make the ancient alloy called bronze?

Bronze is a classic alloy made by mixing copper and tin (lata) together to make it strong!
copy.tl:
Anong dalawang metal ang nagkakaisa para gumawa ng sinaunang alloy na bronze?

Ang bronze ay isang alloy na gawa sa paghahalo ng copper at tin (lata)!
copy.bis:
Unsa nga duha ka metal ang nagkahiusa aron makahimo sa karaang aloy nga bronze?

Ang bronze usa ka aloy nga hinimo sa pagsagol sa tumbaga (copper) ug tin (lata)!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Buko is a young coconut with clear, sweet water inside
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a young coconut and its water, but does not mention or teach the outer parts of plants (leaves, roots, stems) or their role in getting water and nutrients from the soil. It only relates to a plant product, not the plant parts or their functions.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: clear, sweet water inside
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water, which is a liquid, but does not identify or compare the three states of matter (solid, liquid, gas). It does not directly support the competency of identifying that matter exists in three states.

copy.en: Buko is a young coconut with clear, sweet water inside—a refreshing drink, especially on a hot day!
copy.tl: Ang buko ay batang niyog na may malinaw at matamis na tubig sa loob—isang nakakapreskong inumin lalo na sa mainit na araw!
copy.bis: Ang buko mao ang batan-ong lubi nga adunay tin-aw ug tam-is nga tubig sa sulod—usa ka makapreskong ilimnon ilabina sa init nga adlaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A bullet from a rifle can travel super fast at about 1,000 meters per second.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an example of a speed value but does not explain that speed is how far an object moves in a given time. It does not directly teach the definition or concept required by the competency.

copy.en: Zoom! A bullet from a rifle can travel super fast at about 1,000 meters per second.
copy.tl: Zoom! Ang isang bala mula sa riple ay maaaring lumipad nang napakabilis, humigit-kumulang 1,000 metro kada segundo.
copy.bis: Zoom! Ang usa ka punglo gikan sa riple makalupad og super bilis, mga 1,000 ka metro kada segundo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: making its average density less than water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses density and buoyancy, not the definition of matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. Density is a property of matter but the card does not directly support the competency's stated concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Shape matters more than the material!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions shape and material but does not describe physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. It focuses on buoyancy and density, not the properties listed in the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: traps air, making its average density less than water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card references air and water but does not identify the three states of matter (solid, liquid, gas) or teach that matter exists in these states. The mention of air and water is incidental to the buoyancy concept.

copy.en: A concrete boat can float if its hollow shape traps air, making its average density less than water. Shape matters more than the material!
copy.tl: Lumulutang ang bangkong semento kung blangko ang hugis nito para makahuli ng hangin, kaya mas mababa ang average density kaysa tubig. Mas mahalaga ang hugis kaysa materyales!
copy.bis: Makalutaw ang bangkong semento kon blangko ang hugis niini aron makadakop og hangin, busa mas ubos ang average density kaysa tubig. Mas importante ang hugis kaysa materyal!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the air makes your body lighter than water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions air and water but does not teach that matter exists in three states (solids, liquids, gases). It only uses air and water as examples in a buoyancy context, not as states of matter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You float more easily when your lungs are full of air
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the effects of gravity to the motion of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses floating, which involves gravity and buoyancy, but it does not observe or describe the effects of gravity on the motion of an object. It explains buoyancy via density/air, not gravity's effect on motion.

copy.en:
Why is it easier to float when you take a deep breath?

You float more easily when your lungs are full of air, because the air makes your body lighter than water!
copy.tl:
Bakit mas madaling lumutang kapag huminga ka nang malalim?

Mas madaling lumutang kapag puno ng hangin ang baga, dahil ang hangin ay nagpapagaan sa katawan kaysa sa tubig!
copy.bis:
Nganong mas sayon nga molutaw kon magginhawa ka og lawom?

Mas sayon nga molutaw kon puno og hangin ang baga, kay ang hangin naghimo sa lawas nga mas gaan kaysa tubig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: salt water is denser
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions salty seawater, which is a solution, but it does not describe uniform or non-uniform mixtures, solutions, or suspensions. It only states that salt water is denser and that objects float more easily in it, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: salt water is denser
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to density, which relates to mass and volume, but it does not describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. It provides no instructional support for the definition of matter.

copy.en: Things float more easily in salty seawater than in fresh water, simply because salt water is denser!
copy.tl: Mas madaling lumutang ang mga bagay sa maalat na tubig-dagat kaysa sa tubig-tabang, dahil mas mataas ang densidad ng tubig-alat!
copy.bis: Mas sayon nga molutaw ang mga butang sa parat nga tubig-dagat kaysa sa tubig-tabang, kay mas dasok ang tubig nga asgad!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Submarines rise and dive by controlling water in their ballast tanks.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water and air but does not describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. It focuses on buoyancy control, not the definition or properties of matter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Submarines rise and dive by controlling water in their ballast tanks.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure accurately the distance and time when things move using simple equipment
assignedReviews.reason: The card contains no measurement of distance or time, nor any use of simple equipment for measuring motion. It is unrelated to the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When the tanks are full of water, the submarine sinks; when full of air, it rises!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to water and air as substances but does not identify the three states of matter (solid, liquid, gas) or classify them. The mention of water and air is incidental to the buoyancy explanation.

copy.en: Submarines rise and dive by controlling water in their ballast tanks. When the tanks are full of water, the submarine sinks; when full of air, it rises!
copy.tl: Ang mga submarine ay umaahon at lumulubog sa pamamagitan ng pagkontrol ng tubig sa kanilang ballast tanks. Kapag puno ng tubig, lumulubog ito; kapag puno ng hangin, umaahon!
copy.bis: Ang mga submarine motaas ug molunod pinaagi sa pagkontrol sa tubig sa ilang ballast tanks. Kung puno sa tubig, molubog kini; kung puno sa hangin, motaas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A burnay has a narrow mouth so food won't spill and dirt can't get in!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in solid materials make them useful, such as when they are shaped, pressed, hammered, joined, or cut
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a functional design feature of a burnay jar (narrow mouth for spill prevention and freshness) but does not describe how changes in solid materials (shaped, pressed, hammered, joined, cut) make them useful. It shares the broad topic of materials but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: A burnay has a narrow mouth so food won't spill and dirt can't get in! It is also easy to cover to keep the food inside fresh.
copy.tl: Makitid ang bibig ng burnay para hindi madaling matapon o mabuhusan ng dumi ang laman! Madali rin itong takpan para manatiling sariwa ang pagkain sa loob.
copy.bis: Gamay ang baba sa burnay aron dili dali mausik o masudlan og hugaw ang sulod! Sayon usab kining taklupan aron magpabiling presko ang pagkaon sa sulod.
